questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary condition for the Weak Law of Large Numbers to hold?

answers.b: Random variables must have finite variance
answers.c: Random variables must have a finite mean

explanations.c: WLLN requires the random variables to be i.i.d. with finite expected value $\mu$.

questions.question: Which type of convergence does the Weak Law of Large Numbers (WLLN) guarantee?

explanations.c: The WLLN states that the sample average converges in probability to the expected value $\mu$.

questions.question: In the experiment with shrinking intervals (moving rectangles), what is the primary reason the sequence does not converge almost surely?

answers.a: The sample mean converges to a wrong value
answers.b: Each point ω lies in infinitely many non-overlapping intervals
answers.d: The random variables are not identically distributed

explanations.b: Each $\omega$ lies in infinitely many of the shrinking intervals with positive probability, causing infinite fluctuations and hence preventing almost sure convergence.

questions.question: Suppose $X_n \xrightarrow{a.s.} X$. Which of the following must be true?

answers.a: There exists a subsequence of $X_n$ that converges in mean to $X$
answers.b: Every subsequence of $X_n$ converges in probability to $X$
answers.d: $X_n$ converges in distribution to a constant

explanations.b: Almost sure convergence implies convergence in probability. Hence, every subsequence also converges in probability to $X$.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences converges in probability to $0$?

answers.b: $X_n = 1$ if n is even, $0$ if n is odd

explanations.d: In both (a) and (c), the probability of deviating from 0 vanishes as n increases, so $X_n \rightarrow 0$ in probability.
